items.body:
<details open>

metal : fix GROUP_NORM for ne03 > 1 and non-contiguous inputs (#31852)

The kernel_group_norm_f32 kernel and its host dispatch ignored the
batch dimension (ne03) of the source tensor: only ngrp threadgroups
were dispatched and each normalized the flat range
[tgpig*gs, (tgpig+1)*gs) with gs = ne00*ne01*ceil(ne02/ngrp). For
tensors with ne03 > 1, all but the first ne00*ne01*ne02 elements were
left unwritten (exposed by the new GROUP_NORM test with
ne=[3,1,1,65537], num_groups=1).

Dispatch one threadgroup per (group, i03) pair (ngrp in x, ne03 in z,
same work distribution as the Vulkan backend) and compute per-batch
statistics, matching the CPU reference. Also clamp the group element
count for the last group when ne02 is not divisible by ngrp and use
int64_t indexing.

The kernel now only requires ggml_is_contiguous_rows(op->src[0])
instead of full contiguity: it addresses src0 and dst with their own
strides (nb03 and the dst strides are added to the kernel args - dst
can be a strided view of src0 with ggml_group_norm_inplace) and falls
back from the flat fast path to a strided path that decodes the linear
element index when rows or channels are padded. The flat/strided
selection is done on the host in
ggml_metal_library_get_pipeline_group_norm and compiled into one of
two specialized pipeline variants via a FC_group_norm_flat function
constant, so the dead path is eliminated at pipeline creation.
GROUP_NORM support is also gated on F32 src and dst in supports_op -
the kernel only implements f32 and an f16 input would silently be read
as f32.

Assisted-by: dsh:llama.cpp/ggml-org/GLM-5.3-Flash-GGUF (Mac Studio, M5 Ultra, 256GB)

</details>

items.body:
<details open>

server: visit parent slots before child slots (#30779)

* server: visit parent slots before child slots
A parent slot wakes its waiting child slots once it finishes the shared
prompt prefix, while slots are visited in id order. When a child task
lands on a lower slot id than its parent, the child is visited before
the parent wakes it and waits an extra batch to process its suffix.
Non-child slots are now visited before active child slots, so every
child woken by its parent joins the same batch.

* server: check systemone test events through test tags

The systemone tests matched free-form debug messages, including the
formatted f_keep value of the prompt cache. The server now emits
__TEST_TAG_WAIT_PARENT_SLOT__ when a child slot waits for its parent,
__TEST_TAG_PROMPT_CACHE_RESTORE__ on every prompt cache restore and
__TEST_TAG_PROMPT_CACHE_FULL_RESTORE__ when the whole cached prompt is
a prefix of the new one, compared on token counts.

---------

Co-authored-by: Pascal <admin@serveurperso.com>

</details>
